Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + ask: TTFT targets and streaming preferences

Hi Riya — thanks again for the demo today, appreciated the clarity on your ingestion patterns. Quick recap and two asks so we can size the pilot properly: 

Recap (5m):
- Workload: mix of short (user prompts ~40-120 tokens) and long-form (reports ~800-2,000 tokens).
- Peak expected steady-state: ~200 req/s with short bursts to 450 req/s during market open.
- Current integration plan: SSE for push updates to clients, fallback to WebSocket if client needs bidirectional.

Asks:
1) Can you confirm your TTFT SLOs (median / 95th / max acceptable)?
2) Do you have a preferred chunk cadence (e.g., every 80 tokens or time-sliced like 150ms)?

Attached is a draft pilot plan and a simple pacing grid that maps request shapes to concurrency assumptions. If you can reply with the SLO numbers and any latency windows we’ll lock the pilot sizing and a tentative start date (week of 6/14).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Ben and Karthik for the ops sizing once we have your targets.

—Priyom

From: Riya Shah <riya.shah@catalystfinance.com>

Cc: Catalyst Platform Team <platform@catalystfinance.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: TTFT targets and streaming preferences

Priyom — great session, thanks. Answers below so you can proceed: 

SLOs:
- Target (median): <= 220 ms TTFT for short prompts (40–120 tokens).
- P95: <= 420 ms.
- Absolute maximum acceptable (for 99th in peak): 900 ms — anything beyond we consider a degraded UX.

Throughput / concurrency assumptions:
- Steady state: 200 req/s.
- Peak bursts: 400–450 req/s for ~3–6 minute windows around market open/close.
- Concurrent sessions: expect ~60 concurrent long-form sessions and ~300 concurrent short-prompt connections during peak.

Streaming preference:
- Prefer SSE for server-to-client streaming.
- Chunk cadence: prefer token-batched chunks ~100 tokens or time-sliced at ~120ms (whichever yields lower latency). We can be flexible in the pilot.

Security note: we need basic SOC2 evidence and TLS cert pinning support for the public endpoints (we’ll send the questionnaire next).

Riya
Riya Shah
Head of Platform, Catalyst Finance
ri ya.shah@catalystfinance.com | +1 212 555 0987
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT inputs from Catalyst — ops notes and pilot mapping

Thanks Riya (and Priyom) — putting ops perspective here. Key takeaways & what we’ll run in the pilot: 

1) Sizing: to meet median <=220ms and P95 <=420ms at 200 steady / 450 burst, we should run a dedicated pilot pool: 8x A100-equivalent slots with burst headroom. That maps to ~40 concurrent model contexts for long-form + continuous batching for short prompts.

2) Streaming: we’ll default to SSE for the pilot with WS fallback. We’ll instrument chunk cadence as a parameter in the pilot (two arms):
   - Arm A: token-batched chunks ~100 tokens
   - Arm B: time-sliced at 100–150ms intervals
We’ll measure TTFT and perceived completion rate and recommend the winner after 48h of traffic.

3) Priming & KV cache: we’ll enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts to shave ~30–60ms on short prompts.

4) Telemetry: we’ll provide token-level latency, per-route P50/P95, and a synthetic heartbeating trace for each session. Link to the draft metrics schema attached.

Next steps:
- Priyom: confirm pilot start week (Catalyst said flexible week of 6/14).
- Karthik + Ops: prepare runbook for the two-arm cadence test.
- Riya: send SOC2 questionnaire and cert pinning requirements.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Confirming pilot week & items for kickoff (week of 6/14)

Riya — thanks for the clear SLOs. We’ll lock the pilot for the week of 6/14. High-level kickoff checklist below; I’ll send calendar invites after you confirm availability for a 30m kickoff on Mon 6/14 09:00 PT.

Kickoff checklist (pilot week of 6/14):
- Redwood: provision 8x A100-equivalent pilot pool; enable prefix caching; prepare two-arm cadence test (token-batched @ ~100 tokens vs time-sliced @ 120ms).
- Redwood: share runbook + telemetry dashboard link before kickoff.
- Catalyst: provide SOC2 questionnaire answers, cert-pinning details, and a test key for non-prod.
- Catalyst: confirm expected traffic shape for the 48h belt test (CSV or synthetic generator config).

Deliverables by kickoff: pilot runbook (attached), pacing-grid spreadsheet, and a short confluence note that maps SLOs to observability widgets.

If Monday 6/14 09:00 PT works, I’ll send an invite to the Catalyst platform team and our ops leads (Ben, Karthik, Lauren).

Cheers — looking forward to getting this running.

—Priyom
